# Use a PyArrow Table

Whittaker uses [Narwhals](https://narwhals-dev.github.io/) for data ingestion, which means that
`fit()` accepts any DataFrame format Narwhals supports (Pandas, Polars, and PyArrow Tables) all
without any conversion step on your part. This is useful when data arrives from Arrow-native sources
such as Parquet files, Flight streams, or DuckDB queries.

## Build a PyArrow Table

Load the `wages` dataset as a plain dict of NumPy arrays, then wrap it in `pa.table()`. The
resulting PyArrow Table can be passed directly to `fit()`.

::: {#1c177d31 .cell execution_count=1}
``` {.python .cell-code}
import pyarrow as pa
import whittaker as wk

# Load dataset and wrap in a PyArrow Table
data = wk.load_dataset("wages")
table = pa.table(data)
```
:::


Inspect the schema to confirm the columns and their Arrow types.

::: {#f4baf35a .cell execution_count=2}
``` {.python .cell-code}
table.schema
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2}
```
age: double
experience: double
wage: double
```
:::
:::


## Fit using the PyArrow Table

Pass the table to `fit()` exactly as you would a dict or a Pandas DataFrame. Narwhals handles the
translation internally so no `.to_pandas()` or `.to_pydict()` call is needed.

::: {#0c73c7cb .cell execution_count=3}
``` {.python .cell-code}
model = wk.GAM("wage ~ s(age) + s(experience)", family=wk.Gamma()).fit(table)
model.summary()
```

## Inspect model outputs

The fitted model is identical to one trained on a dict or a Polars DataFrame. Effective degrees of
freedom and deviance explained are unaffected by the data format used at fit time.

::: {#4c02823e .cell execution_count=4}
``` {.python .cell-code}
model.edf_total
```


:::

## From an Arrow-native source

In practice, PyArrow Tables often come from Parquet files or DuckDB result sets. The pattern is the
same: no intermediate conversion is required.

::: {#cff185eb .cell execution_count=6}
``` {.python .cell-code}
# import duckdb
# table = duckdb.sql("SELECT age, experience, wage FROM 'wages.parquet'").arrow()
# model = wk.GAM("wage ~ s(age) + s(experience)", family=wk.Gamma()).fit(table)
```
:::


The column names in the Arrow Table become the predictor names used in the formula. Whittaker reads
only the columns referenced in the formula, so the table may contain additional columns without
error.
